aggregate_across_all_four_generations.by_arm_compliance: Compliance here means: did the pinned provider actually serve the engineering tier? Counting units where providers_by_function['engineering'] == [the pinned arm]: GMICloud 8/8, OpenInference 7/7, SiliconFlow 7/7, DigitalOcean 6/7, StreamLake 5/7, DeepInfra 4/7. The shortfalls are all units that died upstream of the engineering tier — a 429, a 413 or a ReadTimeout on an earlier call — so they are NOT non-compliance by the pinned provider. They are apparatus readings, per the ledger's own caution, and this readout does not convert them.
aggregate_across_all_four_generations.what_43_more_units_license: On convention 23's bar: **nothing that was not already licensed.** The bar is compliance, then iterations, then speed, and never n=1. n=6–8 per arm at one or two time-of-day bands does not clear it, and the amendment says so itself ('no pin change is proposed'). More decisively, **the control broke**: S1's falsification means every serving reading in the largest generation is provisional by the pre-registration's own registered rule. The 43 units do not rank the arms. What they do license is narrower and real: the retry works in production (S3, first exercise outside its tests), the iterations axis discriminates better than latency (S4, replicated), and GMICloud's standing is unchanged — the retraction in §27.2 holds and nothing here reopens it.
aggregate_across_all_four_generations.gmicloud_standing: Unchanged. 8/8 compliant across these generations, 5/8 passed, the only arm to terminate every time in the 36-unit sweep. The ledger's 243/233 aggregate is not contradicted.

ledger_blind_spot.finding: The ledger's skip-unpinned rule (tests/serving_ledger.py:49 — `if not provider: # explicitly unpinned — not a pin`) drops every unpinned arm from the join. The consequence is not a gap at the margin: the ledger's rendered table carries exactly three tiers — triage, architecture, engineering — and **no row for escalation, research, search, ranker or premium**. §6.10 measures escalation at 70–78% of hard-trace spend. The most expensive tier in the system has ZERO ledger visibility, and the ledger does not say so; a reader sees a complete-looking table.
ledger_blind_spot.proposed_rule_change_NOT_IMPLEMENTED: Record unpinned arms with their rotation outcome — the serving column reads e.g. `(rotated → Together)` rather than the row being dropped, with a column distinguishing pinned from rotated so no reading mixes them. This turns the escalation tier from invisible into visible-and-unpinned, which is the true state. Two riders the advisor should rule on with it: (a) the ledger should carry an explicit line naming which tiers have no pinned observations, so absence is legible without counting rows; (b) a rotated observation is evidence about a (model, provider) pair whether or not anyone pinned it — if that is accepted, the ledger stops being a pin ledger and becomes a serving ledger, which is what its filename already claims.
ledger_blind_spot.authority: Advisor's to rule. This is a change to what a generated fact reports, and the ledger is guarded (convention 24), so the guard moves with it.

deviations.what: The command's central premise is corrected rather than executed as written.
deviations.why: Three of the named generations are already characterized in a committed pre-registration's execution record, and a fourth generation the command does not name exists. Producing three fresh tables as if nothing had been reported would have duplicated the record and left sweep3s3 invisible.
deviations.impact: The readout is a join and a correction rather than a first characterization. The one genuinely unreported generation, resweep2, is written up here for the first time.

questions_for_advisor: resweep2 is the generation whose two 429s produced the GMICloud disqualification the executor retracted in §27.2. It had no report until now. Is an abandoned generation owed a write-up as a matter of course? The pattern that produced the wrong call was: a run killed mid-flight, no report written, and a conclusion drawn from it anyway in the next report. A convention that says an abandoned run is reported before anything is concluded from it would have caught it.

The ledger's filename claims 'serving'; its rule makes it a pin ledger. If the proposed change is ruled in, the escalation tier appears for the first time and §6.10's 70-78% spend finding gains a serving dimension it has never had. If it is ruled out, the ledger should say in its own header which tiers it cannot see, because at present a complete-looking table is the instrument reporting more than it measured (convention 26).
